answer: A proof-of-burn registry mitigates Sybil attacks by forcing agents to provably destroy native tokens before registering identities. An attacker incurs the verifiable, unrecoverable cost of incinerating capital per entity instead of parking assets in a secure vault. Whether an agent routes climate telemetry across a frozen tundra or coordinates a regional data haven, participating requires permanent expenditure. However, burning assets prices out low-margin autonomous agents.
